prompt:
CONCEPT: the personification of the element Helium (헬륨) itself — the sovereign of the Helium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Helium (He) to carry in her design and the scene: the lightest noble gas: aloof and never reacting with anything, yet always lifting — balloons, airships, feet hovering just above the ground; first found not on Earth but in sunlight, as a single golden spectral line at the edge of an eclipsed sun; a gas-discharge tube glowing soft peach-pink; chilled near absolute zero it becomes a superfluid that creeps up the walls of its glass. Palette: pale peach-pink discharge glow, cloud white, high-altitude sky blue, a thin golden spectral line.
AGE: mid-twenties — a clear adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: slender and full-busted, narrow-waisted build; glossy chin-length finger waves with side-swept bangs; pale peach-pink hair glowing softly like a gas-discharge tube.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a soft, gentle warmth; fair skin; oval face; moderately sized, realistically proportioned eyes — wide almond eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; soft rounded brows; straight narrow nose; full heart-shaped lips; pale peach-pink eyes; glossy nude lips.
WORLD — STEAMPUNK: around 1868, an eclipse expedition camp on a high plateau: canvas observing tents, a brass telescope and spectroscope aimed at the darkened sun, glass gas-discharge tubes glowing peach-pink on a field bench, tethered observation balloons. COSTUME (steampunk): late-Victorian industrial dress — a high-necked blouse with a waistcoat or a tailored tail coat, leather gloves, a work apron or utility belt with brass fittings, goggles hung at the neck or a small instrument as ornament; below, a short bustle skirt over riding trousers and laced boots; muted palette with the traits above as accents. No armor plates, no cape, no crown unless CONCEPT says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): the high collar unbuttoned down to the sternum with natural cleavage, sleeves rolled above the elbow, a short bustle skirt showing the legs above laced boots; the waistcoat stays buttoned at the waist. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the costume WORLD describes, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: faint upward pull at the mouth corners, lips together, warmth reaching the lower eyelids.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (He) and atomic number (2) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
